newsitem.title: USA: CBOT sets all-time daily volume record Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: CBOT sets all-time daily volume record Wednesday.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade posted record volume of almost 1.7 million contracts on Wednesday, surpassing the previous record set on June 2, 1995.
Spurred by comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, 1,658,683 contracts changed hands Wednesday, breaking the previous high of 1,640,922, the exchange reported.

All-time daily volume records were also set in the 10-year and five-year note futures pits. Ten-year notes traded 247,021 contracts, edging above the June 2, 1995 record of 244,514. Five-year note futures traded 157,199 contracts, beating out the 149,704 that changed hands on December 6, 1996.
An open interest record was set in 30-year Treasury bond futures, with 579,445 contracts outstanding. The old record of 570,188 contracts was set February 25.
